circuit_64 - 24 components, 12 nets. Five inverting op-amp stages, each with the feedback element (1uF cap or 1uH inductor) drawn as a rectangle from the output back to the UPPER-left input, and each op-amp's LOWER-left input marked '+'. All five drawn '+' marks sit on the lower input and all five '-' marks on the upper input; the negative-feedback path always lands on the upper input, so the drawn marks and the physical reading agree everywhere - no op-amp needed a guess.

JUDGEMENT CALLS AT INTERSECTION SITES
This drafter marks every real connection with a heavy solder dot, and there is not a single hop, jog or plain X anywhere on the sheet, so all twelve critical sites are junctions. Recorded explicitly:
S24 (457,532) deg=4 dot=2.9 -> JUNCTION. The only 4-way crossing in the drawing: the y~530 rail crosses the long x~457 column. There is an unmistakable filled blob at the centre, roughly 3x the stroke width in both axes, and no hop or jog on either run. The other reading (crossing) would split n5 into {op-amp#14 out, inductor#13 right, resistor#12 left} and {op-amp#3 in+, capacitor#21 left}, i.e. op-amp#3's non-inverting input and capacitor#21 would be driven by nothing at all and op-amp#14's output would no longer reach either. The dot settles it, and the split reading also makes no circuit sense.
S7 (156,196) dot=2.5, S8 (368,200) dot=2.1, S10 (618,200) dot=2.7, S11 (829,215) dot=2.6, S23 (386,530) dot=2.1, S26 (993,530) dot=2.5, S32 (208,585) dot=2.8, S38 (575,817) dot=2.1, S39 (789,848) dot=2.2 -> JUNCTION. Each is a clean T carrying a heavy dot: a feedback wire or a rail terminating on a signal run.
S22 (617,521) dot=1.1 and S25 (803,529) dot=1.4 -> JUNCTION. These two carry no dot, but they are plain Ts where the feedback rectangle's vertical side comes down and ends on the op-amp input/output run - there is nothing passing through, so 'crossing' is not even expressible. Reading them as 'none' would strand the 1uF#9 feedback capacitor on two dead ends.
Non-critical sites S0, S1, S2, S3, S6, S12, S15, S17, S20, S28, S29, S34, S36 are all handwritten value text ('1uF', '1kOhm', '1uH', '5V', '10A') brushing a wire or a symbol; left at defaults, they change nothing.

CLASSES
No class looks wrong. Five triangles with + and - marks = Op-Amp; three coils = Inductor; three plate pairs = Capacitor; five zig-zags = Resistor; circle with +/- bars = V-DC; circle with an up arrow = I-DC; six three-bar symbols = GND.

NOT FULLY RESOLVED
Nothing. Every site carries either a solder dot or an unambiguous T, and every op-amp's +/- marks are legible at 3x, so no terminal needed the fallback physical reading.
